title.en: Circular shaft torque and distributed twist

summary: Expose the load-dependent relative rotation along a circular shaft instead of rotating it as one rigid prop.
objective: Expose the authoritative model and its visible response: circular shaft torque and distributed twist.
applies_when: Uniform solid circular shaft, one end fixed, static end torque, homogeneous isotropic linear elasticity and small shear strain; no distributed torque.
intent_signals: Expose the load-dependent relative rotation along a circular shaft instead of rotating it as one rigid prop.
example_prompts: Build an inspectable demonstration of circular shaft torque and distributed twist with parameter controls and a reset.
negative_signals: Not noncircular warping, yielding, torsional vibration, shaft rotation dynamics or a strength certification.
not_for: Not noncircular warping, yielding, torsional vibration, shaft rotation dynamics or a strength certification.

principles: End torque creates elastic twist relative to the fixed end; it does not prescribe a rotation rate.
Cross sections remain plane in this circular-shaft model; do not generalize that assumption to arbitrary profiles.
implementation: Own L,R in m, shear modulus G in Pa and signed end torque T in N m. For positive finite L,R,G use J=pi*R^4/2 in m^4, theta(z)=T*z/(G*J) in rad and tau(r)=T*r/J in Pa. z runs from the fixed end to L; torque and rotation follow the right-hand rule about +z.

Deform material markers with cross-section rotation theta(z). Show a fixed collar, end torque arrow and a longitudinal stripe that becomes helical. Mesh rings may aid inspection but must remain attached to one continuous surface.

Changing radius rebuilds J and geometry together. Limit the example to small |T|*R/(G*J) and the chosen elastic range; any display twist multiplier is separately labeled and excluded from stress readouts. Reset restores torque and the undeformed reference.
observable_checks: At z=0 rotation is zero; at z=L it is T*L/(G*J). T=0 removes twist and shear stress.
At fixed T,L,G, doubling R reduces end twist by 16 and surface stress magnitude by 8. Reversing T reverses the stripe twist without changing its magnitude.

known_limits: Not noncircular warping, yielding, torsional vibration, shaft rotation dynamics or a strength certification.
Authored reusable guidance; no solver or rendered artifact has been tested for this record.
creative_affordances: Use a cutaway, restrained ghost reference or annotated section only when it clarifies the modeled relation; a planar diagram remains valid when depth adds no information.

claims.statement: For a uniform circular shaft in linear elastic torsion, cross sections remain plane, angle of twist is T*L/(GJ), and shear stress at radius r is T*r/J. For a solid circular section J=pi*R^4/2.
claims.scope: Uniform solid circular shaft, one end fixed, static end torque, homogeneous isotropic linear elasticity and small shear strain; no distributed torque.

source_refs.locator: Torsional Stresses and Displacements, PDF pages 6–8, equations 10–14 and polar moment J
